color.$description: The light palette. Derived roles (surface, text, border) are references into the neutral ramp, so re-tinting the ramp re-tints every surface with it.

semantic.$description: Status colors. Named by meaning, never by hue.

surface-sunken.$description: Background of elements that sit below the page: table stripes, inset wells.

surface-raised.$description: Background of elements that sit above the page: cards, popovers, menus.

text-muted.$description: Secondary text: captions, helper copy, placeholders.

field.$description: A field's own surface. Neobrut's is white too: the field is identified by its 3px ink border and its hard shadow, not by a tint, which is the genre's whole point.

border-strong.$description: A control's own edge: stronger than `border`, which divides content. A field has to read as a field at a glance.

on-semantic-error.$description: Text on the matching fill. A fill with no foreground cannot be read, which is what this token prevents.

on-semantic-info.$description: Text on the matching fill. A fill with no foreground cannot be read, which is what this token prevents.

spacing.$description: The spacing scale. Every gap, pad and inset is one of these steps.

font.$description: Typography: which face, how large, how heavy, and how open the tracking sits. Neobrut's face is heavy and set in caps, so its ramp sits further open than a text face would.

letter-spacing.$description: How far the letters sit from each other. This theme's labels are uppercase and bold, which closes the word up; opening the tracking is how it gets that air back.

tighter.$description: Only for a display weight at display size, where the ink spread would otherwise blob the counters shut.

tight.$description: A large heading in the heaviest weight, where the strokes have already eaten the sidebearings.

normal.$description: This theme's body setting. Not zero: a bold uppercase face reads as a block of ink at its natural tracking, and a hair of air is what keeps the words apart.

wide.$description: A button label. The open end of the ramp is where this theme lives.

wider.$description: An eyebrow or a category mark, set well clear of the copy it introduces.

widest.$description: A single word carrying a whole section, spaced out until it reads as a shape rather than a sentence.

radius.$description: Corner rounding, from square to fully round.

10.$description: A ghost: in the DOM, gone from the eye.

20.$description: Disabled. Over a flat fill this low the shape is still legible but unmistakably dead.

30.$description: A disabled control whose label still has to be read aloud.

40.$description: The dimmed step: an empty track before it is filled.

50.$description: Half. The step most rules ask for, and the one a theme is most likely to have an opinion about.

60.$description: Muted but still read: a disabled field the reader is expected to transcribe.

70.$description: Secondary content that must survive a bright room or a projector.

80.$description: A hair under full strength, for something that should feel nearly solid.

90.$description: Almost opaque: a scrim that dims what is behind it without appearing to.

100.$description: Fully shown. Named so a rule can say it rather than assume it.

opacity.$description: How much of a thing is shown, as a fraction. The fractions are the same in every theme — a fraction is a measurement, not a preference — but this theme's flat, high-chroma fills lose their punch long before a muted one would, so the steps are named for what each is for over its own surfaces.

breakpoint.$description: Viewport widths where layout steps change.

z-index.$description: Stacking order. Layer, never a magic number at the call site.

motion.$description: How things move and how long it takes.

button.$description: Character: the decisions a theme owns for its buttons. Metrics that every theme would answer the same way are spent in the CSS instead.

weight.$description: The button's own weight. A control carries more weight than the prose around it.

tracking.$description: Label tracking. Slightly tight, because a 600-weight label in a small control needs the width back.

shadow.$description: The resting elevation. A control with no shadow sits on the page rather than in it.

shadow-hover.$description: The hovered elevation. The lift is the hover feedback; without it a pointer tells the reader nothing.

border.$description: Stroke weight. Every control and surface reads `width`, so a theme changes its edge weight in one place; the steps above it are the ladder, and this theme's ladder is short because its base stroke is already the heaviest a hairline gets.

width.$description: The edge this theme draws everything with. There is no thinner step on purpose: a 1px border would look like a mistake here.

width-2.$description: The emphasis edge. One step past the base, and it matches the offset of this theme's resting shadow so a lifted control keeps its geometry.

width-4.$description: The heavy edge: a control that must read as selected from across the room.

width-8.$description: The frame. A block drawn rather than outlined.

focus.$description: The focus ring, shared by every interactive element: buttons, links, fields, summaries and dialogs.

icon.$description: Glyph sizes, from the reader's own root rather than the element they sit in — a step has to be a jump, and an `em` step against 14px prose is 2px.

badge.$description: Character: the decisions a theme owns for its badges. Metrics that every theme would answer the same way are spent in the CSS instead.

edge.$description: The stroke the badge draws around itself, so a small shape holds apart from the page. Zero leaves it a bare fill with no edge.

pill.$description: Fully round reads as a pill; false squares it into a tag.

checkbox.$description: How physical a checkbox is: one scalar driving three inset shadows. Zero is flat and drawn; higher is lit and raised.

switch.$description: How physical a switch is: one scalar driving three inset shadows. Zero is flat and drawn; higher is lit and raised.

avatar.$description: How big an avatar is, as the edge of the square it fills. A theme owns the ladder because the size of a face is a design decision, not a product of some other token.

sm.$description: The size for a face in a list or a comment: it reads beside its label without leading the row.

md.$description: The default: a face beside a name, or a profile header at rest.

lg.$description: A face as the subject of a page: a profile header at the top of a long column.
